analysis.title: Morning Briefing: Futs are higher led by Tech; Desk comments; Fedspeaks today
key_insights: US futures are higher, led by tech, after a five-day SPX slide and a ~6.5% drawdown from the recent peak. SPX +1.1%, NDX +2.1%, RTY +0.5%. Pre-market, all Mag 7 are higher, led by GOOG/L +3.9%, AMZN +2.2% and NVDA +1.8%.
Fed remains fully pricing a 25bp hike at the December meeting. Treasury yields are up 1-2bp across the curve and the 10Y is at 5.085%. The desk still sees a 50bp move in December as unlikely.

A busy Fedspeak calendar today (Hammack, Goolsbee, Barr, Barkin, Paulson) should help clarify the path. The desk says the bigger equity question is how the market prices the Fed path through 2027. The recent repricing for December 2026 and Q1 2027 has been hawkish.

PANW reported a Q1 NGS ARR beat of +$630m and raised the full-year NGS ARR guide. The stock was up ~10% in the regular session with most of cyber and +7% after hours. PANW is buying AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B at 45x ARR.

Consumer flow (Briggs Barton): cyclicals are outperforming defensives, helping retail and travel/cruise. After earnings, TJX rose 10%, TGT 6% and LOW was flat, with positioning shaping the reactions. Flows in TGT and TJX were short covering with no follow-through demand, and buyside pushback was greater on TGT than TJX.

Staples (XLP +18% YTD) are described as hitting a wall as demand stalls after the rally, with fade potential for the group. Flows have skewed to the sell side recently. The XLP rally is attributed to thematic rotation rather than fundamental improvement.

Discretionary and retail positioning is shifting up, but mostly through short covering by PB flow z-scores. In restaurants the L/S ratio is at the 42nd percentile on a 1-year view and the 5th percentile back to 2018.

Tech desk (Brian Heavey): NVDA gave up pre-market gains, which the desk reads as investor focus staying on CEO and regulatory overhangs rather than the current quarter or the FY28 revenue growth guide. CRWV was hit on expectations that NVDA will be more cautious with financing. AMD, AVGO and GOOGL are seen gaining share from a weakened NVDA.

Tech flows are dormant, with HT volumes tracking down 30%. The desk bought ~660m vs. sold $450m in tech system wide, with at least a third of the buying in NVDA. Software continues to struggle on renewed frontier lab concerns.

US Market Intel is Tactically Bullish. Positioning is cleaner and entry points more attractive. Inflation is seen as the primary risk, more for early 2027 than now. The desk finds a 50bp Fed hike in December highly unlikely.

Bear-case risks: another leg lower in AI/tech, a decline in the incremental buyer (retail and buybacks), a hawkish Fed narrative with 17 Fedspeakers this week, and no definitive positioning purge yet. Aggregate US positioning is ~20%-ile and global semis exposure is 80%-ile.

Monetization Menu (Nov 16): move back toward tech with primary exposure to Mag7 and options to play an AI rebound. Prefer cyclicals over defensives ex-tech, and still like Europe for cyclical/value exposure, though a USD surge may temper outperformance.

Dubravko reiterates his YE26 SPX target of 8,000 on $365 EPS at 21.9x, 8.4% above Friday's close. His factor views: favor 12M momentum over 3M momentum, low vol is less compelling, AI upstream is attractive after the positioning flush, and consumer cyclicals remain challenged by affordability.
EU/UK markets are mixed with Italy and Germany leading. Yields are 1-3bp higher and the macro tone is hawkish at the margin after the ECB labor cost index for Q3 accelerated.

earnings_insights: PANW (reported after the 11/18 close): Q1 NGS ARR beat of +$630m and a full-year NGS ARR guide raise. Stock +10% in the regular session and +7% after hours per the desk.

PANW is buying Applied Compute for $4.5B at 45x ARR. Per the WSJ quoted in the report, Applied Compute raised $350 million at a $3.25 billion valuation earlier this month and reported $100 million in run-rate revenue.
NVDA (reported 11/17): the desk calls the FY28 revenue growth guide objectively better than expected, but the stock ceded its pre-market gains.
TJX +10%, TGT +6% and LOW flat after reporting on 11/18. Positioning drove the reactions.
WMT reports pre-market today (11/19). Other US earnings today: INTU, KEYS, ROAD, ROST, WSM.
The report does not state EPS or revenue figures for the 11/17-11/18 prints.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is for a 25bp hike. The desk sees a 50bp move as unlikely and says the recent repricing for December 2026 and Q1 2027 has been hawkish.
If the market came to believe 50bp is necessary, a hiking cycle as shallow as the current pricing looks unlikely. That is a bear-case risk for equities.
Yields are up 1-2bp across the curve pre-market. Last week showed equity resilience to higher yields and bond vol, which the desk says should not be expected to be the norm.

A downside print could fuel the recession narrative, while an inline or stronger print would shift flows back to beta and cyclicals. The report lists the release as Nov 17, and YoY figures were not published due to the Oct 2025 government shutdown.
Keeps the European macro tone hawkish at the margin, with bond yields 1-3bp higher.
+42bps in the morning update. Affordability pressure tied to oil prices is cited as a headwind for consumer cyclicals.
Level at the time of writing, during the bounce attempt.

Hawkish Fed narrative: a hotter Retail Sales print plus hawkish Fedspeak could bring multiple members discussing 50bp, with 17 Fedspeakers this week.
A positioning purge has not yet happened, with US positioning at ~20%-ile and global semis exposure at 80%-ile.
NVDA CEO and regulatory overhangs, with more disclosures possible after Huang's ouster.

Inflation is the primary risk to the equity bull case, more of a problem for early 2027.
Another USD surge could temper European outperformance.
Staples trade is seen as long in the tooth, with AI sentiment ratcheting higher a risk to it.

Tech flows are dormant with HT volumes tracking down 30%. The desk bought ~660m vs. sold $450m in tech system wide.
The desk's recession basket (JPRECES Index) is +15.8% QTD vs SPX -1.2%.
The desk would consider US memory and semis plays via options (Nov 11 Monetization Menu), and options to play a rebound in the AI themes (Nov 16 menu).

tension_points.bull_case: NVDA reiterates capex and financing support, capital markets events trade well, and the JPM APAC Tech Conference (~250 firms) is a positive catalyst. HFs have been sellers for 6 consecutive weeks, so positioning is cleaner. The desk is Tactically Bullish.
tension_points.bear_case: AI/tech takes another leg lower, from NVDA failing to reassure on financing, a delay to capital markets events, or negative pre-announcements. Positioning has not purged definitively, with global semis exposure at 80%-ile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NVDA failing to reassure on AI ecosystem financing, or a delay to expected capital markets events.

tension_points.bull_case: The desk sees a 50bp December move as highly unlikely. Nominal GDP growth and record-high margins mean higher inflation is not a problem for SPX earnings in the near term.
tension_points.bear_case: A hotter Retail Sales print plus hawkish Fedspeak could lead multiple members to discuss 50bp. If the market believes 50bp is necessary, the current pricing of 4x hikes looks too shallow.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hotter Retail Sales print combined with multiple Fed members discussing the potential for 50bp.
